user.title: Connect to the MeterProxy app
user.description: Normally Home Assistant finds the app by itself (Settings > Devices & services > Discovered). For a manual setup the token is printed in the app log.

data_description.host: Hostname of the app, e.g. local-solaredge-meterproxy

hassio_confirm.title: SolarEdge MeterProxy
hassio_confirm.description: Connect Home Assistant to the app **{addon}**? Afterwards add your meters with **Add meter**.

reauth_confirm.title: New token
reauth_confirm.description: The app rejected the token. Copy the current token from the app log.

error.cannot_connect: The app is not reachable. Is it installed and running?

abort.already_configured: This app is already set up

data_description.stale_timeout: A source that sends no new values for this long is reported with 0 W.
data_description.poll_timeout: If the inverter stops reading the meters on a port for this long, the app restarts (at most 3 times in a row). 0 = off.
data_description.update_interval: How often the source sensors are read.

meter.title: Meter towards SolarEdge
meter.description: Each meter appears to the SolarEdge inverter as its own revenue meter with its own device ID. Set up exactly the same values on the inverter (SetApp or http://172.16.0.1) (see documentation).

data_description.name: e.g. Balcony PV
data_description.serial_port: USB-RS485 adapter that is connected to the inverter's RS485 port. Several meters can share one adapter.
data_description.address: Must be unique on the RS485 bus (the grid meter, battery etc. use other IDs) and match the device ID set on the inverter.

advanced.name: Serial and meter settings
advanced.description: The defaults match the inverter's defaults.

data_description.ct_current: Same value as set on the inverter.
data_description.serial_number: Reported to the inverter; any number, unique per meter.

sources.title: Sources of {name}
sources.description:
All sources of this meter are added up.

{sources}

add_device.title: Choose inverter
add_device.description: Any device with a power sensor: inverter, micro inverter, smart plug measuring a plug-in PV system, … The matching sensors are filled in on the next page.

source.title: Sensors of {name}
source.description: Only AC power is required. Without a lifetime energy sensor the energy is calculated from the power. DC/string values and daily counters are not suitable.

data.name: Name
data.invert_power: Production is reported as negative value

data_description.phase: Phase the inverter feeds into. Three-phase inverters: 3P.
data_description.power: Required (with 3P alternatively the three phase powers below).
data_description.energy: Optional, increasing lifetime counter (not a daily value).

three_phase.name: Per-phase values (3P only)
three_phase.description: Missing phase values are derived from the totals.

mqtt.title: MQTT source
mqtt.description: JSON payload with the keys `power_active` (W) and optionally `energy_active` (kWh), `voltage_ln`, `frequency` … – see documentation. The broker of the Mosquitto app is used.

data.name: Name
data.invert_power: Production is reported as negative value

error.address_in_use: This device ID is already used on this adapter by {other}
error.port_params: All meters on one adapter need the same baud rate and parity (see {other})
error.power_required: Please choose the AC power sensor
error.power_required_3p: Please choose the AC power sensor or all three phase power sensors
